title: Articles of Confederation
creator: Continental Congress
theme: confederation; institutional capacity
evidence_role: Direct evidence of the initial federal structure and retained state sovereignty
notes: Use the archival citation and transcript separately; do not treat the NARA contextual essay as primary text.

title: Constitution of the United States
creator: Constitutional Convention
theme: constitutional capacity; union; taxation; commerce
evidence_role: Direct evidence of the powers and representational compromises of the new federal framework
notes: The transcription includes the three-fifths clause and other evidence necessary to analyze unequal incorporation.

title: Northwest Ordinance
creator: Confederation Congress
theme: territorial governance; state admission; expansion
evidence_role: Direct evidence of the institutional method for governing territory and admitting states
notes: Analyze territorial integration together with Indigenous dispossession rather than as administrative expansion alone.

title: Treaty of Paris
creator: United States and Great Britain
theme: sovereignty; territorial extent; diplomacy
evidence_role: Direct evidence of the formal settlement ending the Revolutionary War
notes: Record the complete item landing page before extracting images or text.

title: A map of the British and French dominions in North America
creator: John Mitchell
theme: imperial geography; boundaries; continental scale
evidence_role: Geographic context for the territorial system inherited and contested by the United States
notes: LOC notes that this map was later used in establishing the 1783 boundaries.

title: Western Land Claims and Territorial Organizations, 1783–1812
creator: Albert Bushnell Hart; Francis J. Reynolds
theme: western claims; territorial organization; state formation
evidence_role: Retrospective visualization of overlapping claims and territorial reorganization
notes: This is a later interpretive map, not a contemporaneous 1780s source.

title: Alexander Hamilton Papers
creator: Alexander Hamilton and others
theme: public credit; administration; correspondence
evidence_role: Archival collection for tracing fiscal proposals, correspondence, and implementation
notes: Verify the canonical collection landing page and use item-level records for individual documents.

title: Report on Additional Sums Necessary for the Support of Government
creator: Alexander Hamilton
theme: fiscal capacity; federal administration
evidence_role: Direct evidence from Hamilton’s Treasury-era writings
notes: This is not the First Report on Public Credit; retain the precise title and date.

title: Return of the Whole Number of Persons within the Several Districts of the United States
creator: United States census authorities
theme: population; representation; slavery; territorial baseline
evidence_role: Direct quantitative baseline for population and constitutional apportionment
notes: Counts reflect historical categories and exclusions, including enslaved persons and Indians not taxed; preserve original definitions.

title: 1790 Population Map
creator: United States Census Bureau
theme: population density; settlement geography
evidence_role: Derived visualization of the first census population distribution
notes: Treat as a modern visualization compiled from historical census records.

title: Records of the Continental and Confederation Congresses and the Constitutional Convention
creator: United States federal record creators
theme: constitutional design; confederation; western lands
evidence_role: Archival discovery guide for convention records, votes, plans, and transmitted documents
notes: A discovery record, not itself evidence for a substantive historical claim.

title: Constitution of the United States—A History
creator: National Archives and Records Administration
theme: ratification; Federalist debate; institutional failure
evidence_role: Secondary institutional context and discovery path to related primary documents
notes: Use for orientation and links; cite primary documents for historical claims.

title: An Act to regulate the collection of duties on imports and tonnage
creator: United States Congress
repository_identifier: 1 Stat. 627; Fifth Congress, Sess. III, ch. 22
theme: customs administration; ports; enforcement; federal capacity
evidence_role: Direct legal evidence for the collection machinery governing imports and tonnage
notes: This is principally a collection and administration statute, not merely a tariff-rate schedule; cite sections and page images for specific claims.

title: Annual Report of the Secretary of the Treasury on the State of the Finances
creator: United States Department of the Treasury
institution: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRASER
theme: public finance; revenue; expenditures; debt; customs
evidence_role: Title-level discovery source for annual and special Treasury reports and fiscal tables
notes: Use issue-level records and page citations in analysis. FRASER notes that early years were bound into volumes and that OCR can contain errors.

title: Excerpts from the American State Papers: 1792
creator: United States Department of the Treasury
institution: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRASER
theme: import duties; public revenue; receipts; expenditures
evidence_role: Quantitative primary evidence for early federal revenue, including the net product of import duties
notes: Transcribe from page images and record table title, period, units, and page; use OCR only as a finding aid.

title: Records of the United States Customs Service
creator: United States Customs Service and predecessor offices
theme: customs districts; port operations; vessels; duties; enforcement
evidence_role: Archival discovery guide for operational records behind national customs aggregates
notes: The collection is very large and only partly digitized. Create item- or series-level records before treating any underlying document as evidence.

title: Mercantile collection
creator: Various merchants, firms, and companies
theme: trade; finance; insurance; shipping; merchant networks
evidence_role: Discovery source for private commercial records, especially New York and Philadelphia mercantile activity
notes: Broad synthetic collection compiled from multiple provenances. Create component- or item-level records before using evidence; most access requires an in-person appointment.

title: Gelston and Saltonstall ledger
creator: Gelston & Saltonstall
theme: merchant accounts; New York commerce; regional trade
evidence_role: Firm-level evidence on the accounts of a prominent New York City mercantile partnership
bibframe_alignment: Work; Manuscript; Item; Archival finding aid
notes: The public record is a collection description, not a digitized ledger. Inspect the physical volume before extracting counterparties, commodities, values, or balances.

title: Stewart and Jones records
creator: Stewart and Jones; Jones and Ross; associated creators
source_type: merchant and ship-chandler records; finding aid
theme: ship supplies; accounts; correspondence; New York commerce
evidence_role: Firm-level evidence on merchant and ship-chandler operations during the Confederation and early federal periods
notes: Selected 1776–1783 material is on microfilm, but the collection generally requires in-person access. Separate commercial records from John Jones’s Trinity Church records.

title: Morris & Ludlum letter and order book
creator: Morris & Ludlum; James Ludlum
source_type: merchant letter and order book; finding aid
theme: hardware imports; Atlantic trade; commodities; merchant credit and orders
evidence_role: Firm-level evidence on New York orders to British and southern merchants, with founding-era entries concentrated in 1797–1799
bibframe_alignment: Work; Manuscript; Item; Archival finding aid
notes: The volume later became James Ludlum’s farm and mill ledger. Restrict the founding-period tranche to the firm’s 1797–1799 letters and orders and inspect the physical volume before transcription.

title: Vessel manifests and entrance and clearance records in Records of the United States Customs Service
creator: United States customs collectors and customhouses
theme: vessel movements; ports; cargo; tonnage; masters; customs administration
evidence_role: Primary administrative basis for reconstructing arrivals, departures, cargo processing, and vessel documentation by customs district
notes: The guide identifies relevant functions and series but is not a voyage dataset. Add series-, container-, and item-level identifiers before extraction; survival and digitization vary sharply by port.

title: Civilian Records Relating to Slavery: Records of the United States Customs Service
creator: United States Customs Service and predecessor offices
theme: slave trade enforcement; coastwise voyages; manifests; forced migration
evidence_role: Discovery guide connecting customs records to the federal regulation and documentation of voyages carrying enslaved people
notes: The guide explains inward and outward slave manifests and their fields. Most coastwise manifests postdate the core 1790s window; use them for institutional continuity, not as direct evidence of 1790s voyage patterns.

title: SlaveVoyages: Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database
creator: Multiple scholarly contributors and archival projects
theme: transatlantic slave trade; voyages; vessels; captains; embarkation; disembarkation
evidence_role: Voyage-level structured evidence for the coerced-migration and slave-trading component of Atlantic commerce
notes: A derived and periodically updated scholarly database, not a single archive. Preserve database version or access date, voyage ID, field definitions, and source citations; distinguish documented from imputed values.

title: Voyages: The Transatlantic Slave Trade Database
creator: National Endowment for the Humanities; Emory University project team
theme: database provenance; methodology; voyage variables
evidence_role: Independent institutional documentation of the database’s development, contributors, coverage, and voyage-level fields
notes: Use as provenance and methodological context, not as a substitute for the database records or their underlying archival citations.

title: An Act for laying a Duty on Goods, Wares, and Merchandises imported into the United States
creator: United States Congress
repository_identifier: 1 Stat. 24; First Congress, Sess. I, ch. 2
theme: tariff; sugar; molasses; rum; federal revenue
evidence_role: Direct legal evidence for the initial federal duty schedule, including commodity-specific duties relevant to the sugar complex
notes: The act was later amended and repealed. Extract exact commodity description, unit, rate, effective period, and amendment history rather than treating 1789 rates as constant.

title: Dutilh & Wachsmuth letters and accounts
creator: Dutilh & Wachsmuth and correspondents
source_type: merchant correspondence and accounts; finding aid
theme: Haiti; Philadelphia; Baltimore; sugar; coffee; consignments; Atlantic trade
evidence_role: Firm-level evidence connecting Haitian consignments and sugar commerce to Philadelphia and an unidentified Baltimore shipping merchant
notes: Materials are in French, English, and Dutch and require item-level inspection. The unidentified Baltimore account book must not be attributed without evidence.

title: Rufus & James Backus letters received
creator: Rufus & James Backus and correspondents
theme: French West Indies; vessel seizures; embargo; provisions trade; commercial shock
evidence_role: Contemporaneous firm-level evidence on British seizures, the March 1794 embargo, and disruption of American West Indies commerce
notes: Eight surviving letters form a narrow event sample. Use to document reported disruption and merchant response, not the aggregate magnitude of trade effects.

title: Theodore Barrell letter book
creator: Theodore Barrell
theme: sugar; molasses; rum; West Indies; merchant correspondence
evidence_role: Post-founding comparison evidence for the organization of the sugar, molasses, and rum trade among Norwich, Boston, New York, and the West Indies
bibframe_alignment: Work; Manuscript; Item; Archival finding aid
notes: Outside the core 1790s period. Use only as a later comparison and do not project its relationships backward without supporting evidence.

title: Liebmann collection of American historical documents relating to spirituous liquors
creator: Various creators; compiled collection
theme: rum; molasses; sugar islands; merchants; ship captains; smuggling; taxation
evidence_role: Discovery source for documents linking colonial and early-national rum and molasses commerce to West Indian sugar production
notes: A synthetic thematic collection with material across centuries. Create item-level records and distinguish original documents from later collecting context before use.

title: General Records of the Department of State
creator: United States Department of State and predecessor offices
theme: diplomatic correspondence; consular correspondence; treaties; foreign relations
evidence_role: Archival discovery guide for official instructions, dispatches, notes, consular reports, treaty records, and related early-republic diplomacy
notes: The guide is not substantive evidence. Identify the correspondence series, country, direction, date, microfilm roll or container, and item before citation.

title: The United States and the Haitian Revolution, 1791–1804
creator: Office of the Historian, United States Department of State
theme: Saint-Domingue; Haiti; recognition; aid; refugees; slavery; trade
evidence_role: Orientation to shifts in United States policy and discovery framework for diplomatic and domestic evidence
notes: The Milestones series is retired and no longer maintained. Use it for orientation only; test its narrative against primary correspondence, statutes, fiscal records, and Haitian sources.

title: The Citizen Genêt Affair, 1793–1794
creator: Office of the Historian, United States Department of State
theme: neutrality; France; Caribbean colonies; privateering; debt; commerce
evidence_role: Context for the diplomatic and legal environment surrounding United States policy toward revolutionary France and Saint-Domingue
notes: Do not collapse metropolitan French, colonial Saint-Domingue, and Haitian actors into one French position. Cite primary instructions and correspondence for claims.

title: Treaty of Friendship, Limits, and Navigation between the United States of America and the King of Spain
creator: United States of America and Spain; negotiated by Thomas Pinckney and Manuel de Godoy
theme: Mississippi navigation; New Orleans deposit; boundaries; commerce; security; Native nations
evidence_role: Direct legal evidence of the negotiated boundary, navigation, commercial, and security settlement with Spain
notes: Extract claims article by article. Separate the treaty text from later interpretations and track ratification, proclamation, implementation, and subsequent disputes.

title: Treaty of San Lorenzo / Pinckney’s Treaty, 1795
creator: Office of the Historian, United States Department of State
theme: Spain; Mississippi; New Orleans; boundaries; western settlement; Native diplomacy
evidence_role: Orientation to negotiation context, principal provisions, domestic reception, and consequences for western expansion
notes: The page URL preserves the site’s misspelling of Pinckney. Its account is contextual; claims about Native nations, implementation, and economic effects require primary and non-U.S. evidence.

title: An Act for the establishment and support of Lighthouses, Beacons, Buoys, and Public Piers
creator: United States Congress
repository_identifier: 1 Stat. 53; First Congress, Sess. I, ch. 9
theme: lighthouses; beacons; buoys; public piers; federal infrastructure
evidence_role: Direct legal evidence for federal assumption, support, construction, repair, supply, and supervision of maritime navigation aids
notes: Distinguish authorization and state cession from construction, operation, and navigational effect. Extract later amendments and site-specific appropriations separately.

title: An Act to provide more effectually for the collection of the duties imposed by law on goods, wares and merchandise imported into the United States, and on the tonnage of ships or vessels
creator: United States Congress
repository_identifier: 1 Stat. 145; First Congress, Sess. II, ch. 35; cutter provisions at 1 Stat. 175
theme: revenue cutters; customs enforcement; boarding; search; manifests; coastal jurisdiction
evidence_role: Direct legal evidence for customs enforcement powers and the authorization and duties of revenue cutters
notes: The act begins at 1 Stat. 145; cutter provisions appear later in the chapter, including section 62 at 1 Stat. 175. Cite the precise section and page rather than only the act’s opening page.

title: Records of the United States Coast Guard and predecessor agencies
creator: United States Lighthouse Service, Revenue Cutter Service, Life Saving Service, Coast Guard, and related offices
theme: revenue cutters; lighthouse administration; maritime enforcement; navigation; accounts
evidence_role: Archival discovery guide for founding-era lighthouse correspondence and accounts and Revenue Cutter Service administration and operations
notes: Founding-period cutter logbooks are sparse in the central holdings described: general correspondence begins in 1790, but surviving operational logbooks listed centrally begin in 1819. Quantify archival gaps.

title: Lighthouse Letters
creator: Secretary of the Treasury, Commissioner of Revenue, Lighthouse Service, and correspondents
theme: lighthouse administration; construction; repair; supply; keepers; federal-state transfer
evidence_role: Primary correspondence series for early federal lighthouse administration and implementation
notes: Use roll, volume, date, sender, recipient, and page or frame citations. Correspondence measures administration and reported conditions, not automatically changes in wreck risk or trade.

title: Lighthouse Deeds and Contracts
creator: United States Treasury and lighthouse administrators; state and private counterparties
source_type: microfilm publication; property and contract records
theme: federal property; state cession; lighthouse sites; procurement; construction
evidence_role: Primary legal and administrative evidence for the acquisition and contracting required to establish federal navigation infrastructure
notes: Separate deeds, jurisdictional cessions, construction contracts, and later maintenance records. A deed or contract does not establish completion or operational performance.

title: Circular from Alexander Hamilton to Benjamin Lincoln regarding instructions to officers of the revenue cutters
creator: Alexander Hamilton
institution: National Archives and Records Administration, Boston
repository_identifier: Records of the U.S. Customs Service, Record Group 36
theme: revenue cutters; customs enforcement; officer instructions; federal administration
evidence_role: Direct administrative evidence of Treasury instructions translating the 1790 statute into cutter duties
notes: The regional landing page supplies context but not a stable item URL in the public text. Capture the National Archives Catalog identifier and image-level citation before quoting or coding the circular.

title: Treaty between the United States of America and the French Republic
creator: United States of America and French Republic
theme: Louisiana Purchase; sovereignty; territory; commerce; ports; navigation
evidence_role: Direct legal evidence for the cession, incorporation provisions, and temporary commercial treatment of French and Spanish vessels and merchandise
notes: Analyze article by article. The treaty transferred claimed sovereignty; it did not itself establish effective boundaries, Indigenous consent, administrative control, or increased exports.

title: Convention for payment of sixty million francs to France
creator: United States of America and French Republic
theme: Louisiana Purchase; financing; public debt; international credit
evidence_role: Direct legal evidence for the principal financing terms of the Louisiana acquisition
notes: Keep the purchase price, United States stock issued, interest, exchange, commissions, and claims convention analytically separate when calculating fiscal cost.

title: Louisiana Purchase, 1803
creator: Office of the Historian, United States Department of State
theme: France; Spain; New Orleans; Mississippi; diplomacy; territorial acquisition
evidence_role: Orientation to the diplomatic sequence and financing of the acquisition
notes: Use for orientation only. The headline acreage and price do not measure commercial access, implementation, distributional effects, or effective control.

title: Louisiana: European Explorations and the Louisiana Purchase
creator: Various creators; Library of Congress curators
theme: Louisiana; Mississippi; New Orleans; maps; exploration; colonial administration
evidence_role: Discovery collection for maps, printed material, and contextual evidence on the lower Mississippi and acquisition
notes: Create item-level records for maps and documents. Curatorial essays and later maps cannot substitute for contemporaneous commercial or administrative evidence.

title: Records of the New Orleans Customhouse within Records of the United States Customs Service
date: early federal period onward, series-specific dates vary
creator: Collector of Customs at New Orleans and related customs offices
repository_identifier: Record Group 36; New Orleans customs records
theme: New Orleans; exports; imports; manifests; entrances; clearances; duties; vessels
evidence_role: Primary administrative discovery path for measuring port traffic and trade after the United States assumed control
notes: The national guide is not a series inventory. Identify exact New Orleans series, dates, gaps, containers, and reporting definitions before constructing totals or pre/post comparisons.
